title: Deepavali 2026: Green Crackers Allowed In Delhi-NCR In Two Daily Slots
excerpt: The Supreme Court permitted CSIR-NEERI-certified green crackers on November 7 and 8 between 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. in Delhi-NCR only, with 300-metre no-cracker zones and the full ban returning November 9.
body:
• The Supreme Court has permitted certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR only, on November 7 and 8, 2026, between 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. each day.
  • Only crackers certified by CSIR-NEERI and PESO may be sold or burst; crackers containing barium, series 'ladis' and garlands, and any non-approved cracker remain prohibited.
  • No bursting is allowed within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and notified silence zones, which are designated 'No-Cracker Zones'.
  • The complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR stands restored from November 9, 2026; sales are allowed only at designated locations, not online.

The Supreme Court has temporarily relaxed Delhi-NCR's complete firecracker ban for Deepavali, permitting the sale and bursting of certified green crackers on November 7 and 8, 2026, in two fixed windows each day — 6 a.m. to 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. The permission applies to Delhi-NCR; it is not an all-India rule.

A bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale chose a regulated approach over continuing the blanket ban, finding that the ban had not significantly improved air quality and that conventional firecrackers continued to be sold illegally, including under the guise of green crackers, SCC Times reported in its summary of the order in Arjun Gopal v. Union of India. Diwali falls on November 8 this year, The Pioneer reported.

What is permitted, and where

Bursting is confined to the two stated slots on the two stated days, and only in Delhi-NCR. No firecrackers may be burst within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and notified silence zones; those areas are to be declared "No-Cracker Zones," marked on the ground and published.

Only manufacturers holding valid CSIR-NEERI and PESO certification may make the green crackers listed on the CSIR-NEERI website, manufactured between November 2 and 6, 2026. Green crackers developed by CSIR-NEERI are claimed to produce 30 per cent less pollution than conventional firecrackers, The Pioneer noted. Every box must be sealed and carry a product-specific, non-transferable QR code showing the manufacturer, NEERI registration, licence, formulation and test certificate.

What remains banned

Firecrackers containing barium and any cracker not approved by CSIR-NEERI as a green cracker remain prohibited, as do joined series crackers ('ladis') and garlands. Traders' cancelled licences were restored temporarily from November 4 to 6, 2026, only to sell approved green crackers bought from certified manufacturers, and any violation brings immediate cancellation. Manufacturers and traders must furnish monetary security, forfeited on violation.

District collectors and commissioners, with district police chiefs, designate the locations where green crackers may be sold across Delhi-NCR. Sale anywhere else, including through online platforms, is prohibited. Patrolling teams are to inspect sale points, verify QR codes at random, confiscate illegal or conventional crackers and prosecute offenders, and authorities must check vehicles entering Delhi-NCR for illegal firecrackers.

Monitoring, and the ban's return

The Central Pollution Control Board, with state pollution control boards, must monitor AQI readings and prepare pre-Diwali reports for November 2-6, Diwali reports for November 7-8 and post-Diwali reports for November 9-30, 2026, including sand and water samples. State authorities must file compliance affidavits, including hospital admission data through November 30, by December 14, 2026, and the matter is listed for compliance on December 16, 2026.

The court held that the right to practise religion under Article 25(1) is subject to public order, morality and health, and that Article 21 includes the right to a healthy, pollution-free environment. From November 9, 2026, the complete ban stands restored across Delhi-NCR. Readers outside Delhi-NCR should check their own state and city rules: this order does not set their time slots.

nri_angle: For diaspora families with homes or relatives in Delhi-NCR, the order sets the only lawful celebration windows this Deepavali — certified green crackers, 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. on November 7-8 — and does not extend to other Indian states or cities.
